data.title: Tacrolimus ointment (0.03%, 0.1%)
data.summary: IX Immunomodulators · Topical calcineurin inhibitor (TCI); macrolide from Streptomyces tsukubaensis
data.body:
_Topicals · IX Immunomodulators_

**Class:** Topical calcineurin inhibitor (TCI); macrolide from Streptomyces tsukubaensis

## Mechanism of action
- Binds FKBP-12 inside T cells; the complex inhibits calcineurin → NFAT not dephosphorylated → less IL-2, IL-4 and other cytokines
- Also reduces mast-cell and basophil mediator release, and Langerhans cell function
- Does not cause skin atrophy (no effect on collagen synthesis)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Atopic dermatitis (moderate–severe; approved) — face, eyelids, flexures; proactive twice-weekly maintenance
- Vitiligo (face and neck — good response), seborrhoeic dermatitis, intertriginous/facial psoriasis
- Oral and genital lichen planus, cutaneous lupus (facial), steroid-induced rosacea/perioral dermatitis (steroid withdrawal)
- Lichen sclerosus (second line), morphoea, chronic actinic dermatitis

## Dose & formulations
- 0.03%: children 2–15 years (and adults); 0.1%: adults (16 years and older)
- Twice daily until clear, then twice weekly as maintenance
- Off-label use under 2 years is common with 0.03%

## Adverse effects
- Burning, stinging, warmth at application site in the first week (most common; improves)
- Alcohol intolerance (facial flushing after drinking)
- Skin infections: folliculitis, herpes simplex/eczema herpeticum, molluscum, warts
- Boxed warning (FDA 2006) about theoretical malignancy (lymphoma, skin cancer) — long-term studies have not shown a clear increase

## Contraindications
- Immunosuppressed patients, Netherton syndrome (high absorption), active infection at site, malignant/pre-malignant skin lesions
- Children under 2 (label)

## Drug interactions
- Systemic CYP3A4 inhibitors — minimal relevance (low absorption) except with large areas or barrier defects

## Pregnancy & lactation
Minimal absorption; may be used on limited areas if needed.

## Viva points
- Calcineurin inhibitor — no atrophy, so ideal for face and eyelids
- 0.03% for 2–15 years, 0.1% for adults
- Burning sensation and alcohol flushing
- Boxed warning — theoretical malignancy

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.48 (Topical calcineurin inhibitors); Khopkar ch.23 (Topical immunomodulators). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
